Spaarne Gasthuis (Haarlem) Radiology | 18 December 2024 | Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate
Clinical Indication: Reassessment due to rising PSA value: 7.8 ng/mL and a previous positive biopsy.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 47.17 mL in total volume. T2-weighted sequences identify an asymmetric hypointense area within the left peripheral zone spanning the base to mid section, sized roughly 14 x 11 x 16 mm. DWI reveals restricted diffusion with matching low ADC signal, categorizing this finding as PI-RADS: 4. DCE sequences highlight early focal enhancement against the background parenchyma. Seminal vesicles appear normal. There is no evidence of extracapsular extension or suspicious lymphadenopathy. The bladder and rectum are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS: 4 lesion located in the left peripheral zone (base/mid).
Prostate volume: 47.17 mL; PSA density: 0.165 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa probability: 0.75055045.

previous_notes.author: Dr. E. Mulder (GP)
previous_notes.text: 16 January 2023 | Dr. E. Mulder (GP): Initial consultation occurred after a June 2022 PSA reading of 6.1 ng/mL. Subsequent testing confirmed the elevation, leading to a urology referral and a biopsy that returned positive for malignancy. Renal function and lipid profiles continue to be tracked alongside his specialist care. Due to residing outside our primary service area, routine telephone check-ins have been arranged.

previous_notes.text: 07 September 2024 | Dr. E. Mulder (GP): Ongoing monitoring for established prostate cancer. Remote communication is preferred given the significant travel distance to the clinic.
